what_is_working: No emoji anywhere, measured rather than assumed. I scanned 3,529 string literals across app/lib, app/web and app/android/app/src/main (382 of them carrying prose) for the Miscellaneous Symbols, Dingbats, Arrows, Emoticons, Supplemental Symbols and flag ranges: zero hits. I scanned the seeded year - 14,061 events over 13 monthly files, 19,165 string fields - for the same ranges: zero hits. evidence/logs/fonts.json shows only three bundled faces (DeskStamp, NoorHand, TeoHand), so there is no emoji font to fall back to either.

The emotional layer is made of rendered physical things, not pictograms. In 01_pulse.png the row at y 1180-1560 is a drawn chair on a torn scrap, an ink scribble, paper confetti, a pinned cloth bundle, a wrapped sweet and a folded note - six objects with their own contact shadows on the wood. evidence/logs/haptics.check.json counts 36 feelings in six families, every name a plain phrase ('a squeeze', 'empty chair', 'i'll make you tea', 'not okay', 'tuesday soup'). Reactions are the same objects, not glyphs: app/lib/regions/chat/note.dart:132-146 lays FeelingObject over the note rather than text.

The messenger's state marks are drawn with a pen, not typed. app/lib/regions/chat/note.dart:326-340 renders queued/sending/sent/read/refused as Mark.clip, Mark.ticks, Mark.tick, two Mark.ticks and Mark.cross; the crops of 13_messenger_states.png at y 1930-2000 and y 2490-2580 show them as ink strokes in the same hand and colour as the writing, with 'it would not go' in red and its cross beside it.

No product-marketing voice in any string the app displays. Across those 3,529 literals: zero exclamation marks in prose (every '!' in the source is a Dart null-assertion inside an interpolation or the '<!DOCTYPE' in a served page), zero instances of the reader being called a user (the one 'user' is 'user-scalable=no' in app/web/index.html:6), and zero self-naming (the three 'lovetap' strings are a MethodChannel at feelings/sensation.dart:40, an HKDF salt at transport/protocol/wire.dart:63 and a MethodChannel at ambient/ambient_stub.dart:9 - none displayed). The home-screen label is 'the other phone'. The push words in app/web/push/sw.js are 'wrote something', 'left their voice', 'is holding something out'. The empty states read 'first one's yours.', 'nowhere planned. that's fine.', 'nothing to do. suspicious.'

No simulated paper, measured four ways. (1) Edges: the nine paper components larger than 150k px in 02_chat.png have top-edge residuals of 10.6 to 38.5 grey-px standard deviation and 139 to 344 px peak-to-peak after removing tilt - torn, not straight and not arced. (2) Corners: the only square-edged surfaces are the cut-card tabs; the CHAT tab's left boundary goes 50 -> 9 -> 8 px in two rows and its top edge holds 0.34 px std, i.e. a 90-degree cut corner, nowhere near the 12-24 px arc a rounded rectangle would draw. (3) Repeat: with row and column structure removed, the paper grain in 05_settings.png (crop 120,1660-1340,1960) autocorrelates 0.88 at lag 2 decaying monotonically to -0.25 at lag 600 horizontally with no lattice peak, and vertically peaks only at lag 88 (r=0.39) and 176 (r=0.29) - the ruled lines and their first harmonic, which is what ruled paper is, not a tile; the wood in 10_first_run.png peaks at r=0.157 horizontally and 0.313 vertically beyond lag 40. (4) Composite: app/lib/material/paper.dart stacks a baked shadow render, a stock, a tear mask and an edge-light render, with no noise overlay anywhere in it, and crops/02_chat_300_edge.png shows broken fibres standing off the tear with the shadow following them.

The counters that exist are records, not scores. 03_us.png shows 'sunday 9 call ... 20 times' at y 1740-1900 and 'to do / 10 open' - quantities of state. app/lib/modules/rituals/rituals_module.dart draws eight weeks of tally strokes with no zero, no gap marker and no colour for a missed week, and app/lib/modules/rituals/thread_row.dart clamps the mark to seven and stamps 'kept'. Nothing anywhere counts consecutive days, warns about a break, or scolds. app/lib/app.dart:341 turns a card's corner down for something unread instead of putting a number on a tab, and app/web/push/sw.js re-shows one tagged notification so arrivals never stack into a count.
verdict: Three of the four forbidden interpretations are absent by measurement rather than by assertion. There is not one emoji glyph in 3,529 code literals or 19,165 seeded string fields, no emoji font is bundled, and the feelings are 36 rendered physical objects with plain-word names; the app's voice carries no exclamation mark, never calls the reader a user and never names itself; and the paper is genuinely torn - nine sheets in one frame with 10 to 38 px of edge noise, cut cards with two-pixel corners, and grain that autocorrelates like paper rather than like a tile, with the only periodicity in it being the rule spacing itself. The rituals surface, which is where engagement machinery would have been easiest to write, counts times and never days-in-a-row, and an unread note turns a corner down instead of wearing a number. What stands against a clean sheet is one thing and it is real: the app has never been given a face. The icon on the home screen and on every notification banner is the Flutter framework's own logo, unaltered since the project was scaffolded, and evidence/crops/reception.png shows it twice on the banner that announces a feeling arriving - a vendor's stock illustration standing where the app's own identity should be, on the one surface the emotional layer reaches while the phone is in a pocket. Below that sit two smaller things: a gold star and a crown still shipped and still offered in the drawer where a person makes a feeling of their own, and two surfaces - the Android first run and the two-phone view - that no artifact shows at all, which leaves the flow where onboarding voice usually hides unexamined. None of these is the catastrophic failure this row is weighted against, and simulated paper in particular is not here, so the category clears its floor; it does not reach ten while the framework's logo is the first thing either of them sees when the other one reaches out.
